RagShortTexts: The Árpád dynasty rebuilt Hungary after the Mongol devastation, erecting a kingdom-wide.

Variants.Content: Árpád stripes and the patriarchal cross flew over the realm, and the Árpád dynasty ruled Hungary under the Holy Crown of Saint Stephen. The 1241 Mongol invasion destroyed the kingdom's field army at Mohi and devastated its plains. King Béla IV, who fled to the Adriatic coast during the invasion, rebuilt the state with stone castles that guarded the Carpathian passes and the Danube crossings. He also reformed the armoured heavy cavalry that had been broken in the battle and brought Cuman horsemen into royal service. The rebuilt defences and the king's diplomacy earned him the title Second Founder of Hungary, though the cost fell on the peasant labour that raised the walls.

Béla tried to bind steppe auxiliaries to the crown through royal marriages, which gave the court a foothold among the horse nomads on the eastern frontier. The Austrian succession pulled the court into a costly struggle with Ottokar II of Bohemia, and the western duchies drained the treasury. A lord near the border had to watch whose letters reached the king first.
Lime kilns burn throughout the Hungarian plain. Villagers find security behind stone curtain walls at Buda and Visegrád, confident that nomad raids will break against masonry.
